question: Where will my CTL be after 4 weeks at 350 TSS/week?

events.content:
Based on a simulation starting from your current metrics, here is what would happen if you maintain 350 TSS per week for the next 4 weeks:

*   **Current Baseline:** CTL 26.4 (Your average load over the last 4 weeks has been about 200 TSS/week)
*   **End of Week 1 (Nov 1):** CTL rises to **30.0** (ATL 37.8, TSB -7.7)
*   **End of Week 2 (Nov 8):** CTL rises to **33.0** (ATL 44.8, TSB -11.8)
*   **End of Week 3 (Nov 15):** CTL rises to **35.6** (ATL 47.4, TSB -11.8)
*   **End of Week 4 (Nov 22):** CTL reaches **37.8** (ATL 48.3, TSB -10.6)

**Simulation Takeaway:** 
After 4 weeks at 350 TSS, your **CTL (Fitness) will sit at 37.8**. 

*Note on assumptions:* This simulation assumes you spread the 350 TSS evenly across 5 training days per week. Because 350 TSS is a noticeable jump from your recent ~200 TSS/week average, your Form (TSB) will drop to around -10 to -12. This is a very standard and manageable level of training fatigue, meaning you'll be putting in solid work without dipping into a high-risk overreaching zone (which typically occurs when TSB falls below -30).
